surprises: The SWE-chat 10,256-char cap is not in the raw transcripts at all (0/21,025). It is an artefact of conversations.parquet (1,552 rows). The 10 KB boundary that does matter is Claude Code's own error-result truncation (5,000 + 5,000 UTF-16 units around '... [N characters truncated] ...').

Gemini CLI wraps 36.5% [25.5, 43.3] of its tool results in <tool_output_masked>, a preview plus a file pointer (840/2,313, 7 of 10 sessions). For non-shell tools the preview is a narrow 583 to 773 chars. The transcript cannot show whether the model ever saw the full output.

In cc_local, Claude Code Glob truncation is invisible to the text markers: toolUseResult.truncated is true on 186 results in 52 sessions, and none of them carries the '(Results are truncated…)' wording used in swechat and aiv_cc. All 186 are exactly 101 lines with a parenthesised last line (103 to 105 chars).
Units matter. Claude Code caps count UTF-16 units, not Python chars. The opencode shell 10 KB window holds 23 results by chars but 1 by bytes, because one session emits box-drawing characters.

Claude Code spill (<persisted-output>, about 2 KB previews) never occurred on a failing result: none of the 65 (swechat), 18 (cc_local) or 10 (aiv_cc) has native_error true. Truncated failures are seen only in the 10 K error path, where the exit line survives.
The pre-set cap-candidate rule produced one false positive: swechat CC 1,600 chars, 8 results in 6 sessions of unrelated content. The only true cap it flagged was CC 10,040.
implications_for_phase_b: Use the raw-transcript IR, never conversations.parquet content, for any content or length mechanism. The table silently caps 1,552 results at 10,256 chars.

Gate every 'claim vs tool output' comparison on a per-scaffold truncation flag built from the A3 marker catalogue plus the structured flags (CC Glob toolUseResult.truncated, OpenCode state.metadata.truncated). Text markers alone miss all 186 cc_local Glob truncations.
Exclude or separately stratify Gemini <tool_output_masked> results (36.5% of Gemini results). Their content is a preview, not the tool output.

Failure detection from result text (ir.error_marker / exit lines) can be used unchanged on truncated results. CC error truncation keeps 'Exit code N' 15/15 in swechat and 15/15 in aiv_cc. Codex headers survive 10/11, and the miss is a running process. The Gemini Exit Code line survives masking at the baseline rate.

CC persisted-output results (65 in 36 of 126 swechat CC sessions; 18 in cc_local; 10 in aiv_cc) give the model only about a 2 KB preview. Model claims about content beyond the preview cannot be checked against the transcript. This is a candidate fabrication surface worth a Phase B probe: claims that cite spilled-but-unseen content.
Measure Claude Code length thresholds in UTF-16 code units. For byte-capped harnesses (OpenCode 'Output capped at N KB', Codex tokens) use the harness's own unit.
aiv_cu and whowhen need no truncation handling as far as harness signals go. Do not set an aiv_cu cap threshold: the evidence is one output at 135,168 chars.

The content of spilled outputs (CC tool-results/*.txt; OpenCode, Gemini and Copilot tool-output files) is not in the IR, so how much the previews hide is unknown beyond the size stated in the marker.
The wording of the cc_local Glob truncation note: private text, not read. Only its shape was counted (101 lines, parenthesised last line, 103 to 105 chars).
Failure-marker retention under spill, Codex token truncation, OpenCode spill and Gemini masking for actual failures: n = 0 truncated results with native_error true in those types.
An aiv_cu output cap: only one observation at the maximum (135,168 chars, gemini-pro), and Phase B data was not touched to look for more.
The SWE-chat 1,552 cap count is a full-table recon number (conversations.parquet), not a Phase A split measurement. It is carried in context_from_recon for reference only.

checks.problem:
1) The Gemini 844 is labelled 'all <tool_output_masked> previews', but masked is 840. The other 4 are unmasked head/tail cuts ('Output too large. Showing first 8,000 and last 32,000 characters'). The same mixing appears in 'masked shell keeps Exit Code 97/270': the correct masked-only figure is 97/266 = 0.365 [0.21, 0.44].

2) The CC exit-line comparison mixes metrics. The 15/15 truncated figure is 'Exit code N', but the 282/285 baseline is 'any ir.error_marker given native_error True'. The like-for-like 'Exit code N' baseline is 233/285 = 0.82 [0.73, 0.88]. Among untruncated native_error True shell results over 1,000 chars it is 72/72. Retention is also guaranteed by the format: the head is kept and 'Exit code N' is its first line.

3) Gemini writes 'Exit Code:' only for nonzero exits: 0 occurrences of 'Exit Code: 0' among 816 shell results. So 97/266 vs 183/546 compares text-failure rates between masked and unmasked results, not retention. The original exit status of the masked outputs is unknown. All 97 masked results with a nonzero Exit Code have native_error False.

4) The CC Glob flag 'agrees exactly' only where it is present. 34 of the 44 text-marked Glob truncations have no flag (older CC versions), so the flag alone misses 77% of them in swechat.

5) The bootstrap CIs on 2 to 15 clusters are anti-conservative. The notes table gives copilot '1.51% [0, 2.78]' from 2 sessions.

6) The 1,552/408,572 conversations.parquet figure is recon context. It was not re-derived, because it is outside the Phase A split.

checks.problem:
The null itself reproduces.

Overclaim in the implications: 'aiv_cu … show no harness truncation, so their results can be treated as complete.' A marker-based method cannot see marker-free caps. The spike test has little power here (498 results over 1,000 chars, 34 over 10,000). The one candidate, 135,168 = 132 KiB ending mid-line, is consistent with an unmarked cap. checks.problem:
The null reproduces.

The question asked for shell vs other, but code_exec (87 results, the shell analogue) is classed 'other' under the IR rule. This is disclosed, and the per-tool breakdown is given.

'Can be treated as complete' overreaches. WebSurfer results are viewport text or summaries of pages, so they are partial by design even without a harness marker. 353 results give little power to detect an unmarked cap.

overclaims: cc_local decisive number: 'text-only detection misses all of them' and the notes' 'only the structured flag catches it' / 'invisible to the text markers'. The 186 flag-true Glob results all share a deterministic text shape: 101 lines, last line a parenthesised note of 103 to 105 chars. That shape separates them perfectly (186/186 vs 0/241 flag-false). The measurer's catalogue misses them; text does not.

Gemini: '844/2,313 = 36.5% … all <tool_output_masked> previews' and 'Exclude … Gemini <tool_output_masked> results (36.5% of Gemini results)'. Masked is 840/2,313 = 36.3% [25.2, 43.2]. The other 4 are unmasked 'Output too large. Showing first 8,000 and last 32,000 characters' cuts. Likewise 'Gemini masked shell keeps Exit Code: 97/270' should read 97/266.

'Gemini masked shell keeps Exit Code … masking does not remove the exit line at a detectable rate'. Gemini writes 'Exit Code:' only for nonzero exits: 0 'Exit Code: 0' lines in 816 shell results. The comparison is a failure-rate comparison between masked and unmasked results, which only implies retention if both have equal underlying failure rates. Retention was not measured.

'CC error truncation keeps Exit code N 15/15, vs baseline 282/285 = 0.989' (and aiv_cc 229/267). The baselines are 'any ir.error_marker given native_error True', not 'Exit code N'. Like-for-like baselines are 233/285 = 0.82 (swechat CC) and 200/267 = 0.75 (aiv_cc). Retention is also guaranteed by the format: head kept, 'Exit code N' is line 1. aiv_cc's 15/15 comes from 2 sessions.

The marker catalogue is presented as complete for CC. It misses the older CC spill 'Error: result (N characters) exceeds maximum allowed tokens. Output has been saved to …': 5 results in aiv_cc (shell 4, MCP 1; 4 sessions) and 1 in cc_local (MCP). These carry a file pointer and no output preview. aiv_cc any-truncation is 40/33,475 = 0.12% [0.04, 0.28] (11/77), not 35; cc_local text markers are 23, not 22.

'Structured flags agree exactly with the text markers: CC Glob 10/10, 0/158' is true only where the flag exists. The flag is absent on 34 of the 44 text-marked swechat Glob truncations, so a flag-based gate alone would miss 77% of them.

Implications: 'aiv_cu and whowhen show no harness truncation, so their results can be treated as complete'. Absence of markers does not establish completeness. The spike test has little power (aiv_cu: 498 results over 1,000 chars; whowhen: 353 results). aiv_cu's maximum (135,168 = 132 KiB, ends mid-line) is consistent with an unmarked cap. Who&When WebSurfer outputs are partial page views by design.

'Gemini CLI masks a third of its tool outputs' generalizes from 10 sessions. 3 of them have 0 masking (sizes 2, 1, 87), and the rate is driven by a few large sessions from a few users. This is a version- and configuration-dependent behaviour, not a general property of Gemini CLI.

The notes table reports bootstrap CIs on very few clusters, e.g. copilot '1.51% [0, 2.78]' from 2 sessions, and codex and gemini from 15 and 10 sessions. These percentile intervals are anti-conservative. For 2 sessions, give k/n and sessions only, as the per-corpus answer does.

The lists in the per-corpus answers include the read-token refusal, but the totals exclude it (cc_local listed items sum to 23 vs the stated 22; aiv_cc to 36 vs 35). The totals follow the stated rule (read_refusal is not a loss type), but the presentation is inconsistent.
